gloss: to get involved in; to try one's hand at; to lay a hand on

definitions.gloss: to get involved in; to try one's hand at
definitions.explanation: To start doing something new or to venture into an unfamiliar area.

definitions.gloss: to lay a hand on; to resort to violence
definitions.explanation: To physically strike or harm someone.

definitions.gloss: to make a move on; to make advances toward
definitions.explanation: To attempt a romantic or sexual approach toward someone.

examples.english: I tried my hand at stocks.

notes:
A versatile idiomatic expression with several distinct meanings depending on context. The literal meaning is "to put out one's hand," and each sense extends this image in a different direction.

USAGE:
- Sense 1 often carries a nuance of recklessness or venturing into something one shouldn't. Frequently appears with negative outcomes.
- Sense 2 specifically means physical violence. The phrase ⟦{先|さき}→先：02883_saki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{手|て}を{出|だ}す (to strike first) is very common.
- Sense 3 implies unwanted or inappropriate romantic/sexual advances.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手|て}を{出|だ}すな: don't touch / don't get involved
- ⟦{先|さき}→先：02883_saki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{手|て}を{出|だ}す: to make the first move (in a fight)
- {手|て}を{出|だ}さない⟦{方|ほう}→方：01139_hou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧: better not to get involved

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{付|つ}ける→付ける：00761_tsukeru⟧: to start on; to meddle with — similar to sense 1 but often implies beginning a task or tampering
- ⟦{手|て}を{貸|か}す→手を貸す：22775_tewokasu⟧: to lend a hand — has a positive connotation of helping, unlike {手|て}を{出|だ}す which often implies recklessness
